licensed_by: kogaki#745 — this carrier holds the CURRENT control plane only. It is not a version ledger: superseded states, defect specimens and the history of past amendments live in git and in the issues. A change is licensed by an issue, settled by a dated owner decision where it is a decision rather than a transcription, landed here, and recorded by bumping `version` and replacing this line with the issue that licensed it. Ratification is a human act: nothing denies an edit no issue licensed, and these two fields gate no code path.

state_kinds.compute: Runs, writes no owner artifact, does not stop.
state_kinds.write: Runs a renderer bound to it and writes exactly one owner artifact. The renderer is private to the executor (§15.5) and renders under the grammar_surface THIS STATE declares, never one bound to the artifact path.
state_kinds.judgment: Reaches a declared judgment point. The judgment arrives as a typed record; the executor validates and never composes it (SPEC §15.6).
state_kinds.wait: The executor stops. Nothing further runs until the owner speaks and the session re-enters (SPEC §15.2, §15.4).
state_kinds.terminal: The run is over. Runs nothing, writes nothing, and the executor stops without awaiting an owner. Distinct from `compute` because a generic interpreter holds no state list of its own (SPEC §15.1) and must read the end from the table rather than from position.

field_semantics.renders_gate_declaration: Required on every state. `true` only where the state renders a gate declaration for AskUserQuestion, and `true` is what SCHEDULES the executor's composition of that state's declaration. It is a statement about the table and never about the runtime asking — §6.3's question allowlist for the post-tag window is empty and stays empty; the executor writes a file and stops.
field_semantics.conditional: Required on every state. `false` where the state is always entered; otherwise a string naming the condition. Counted by counted_baseline.conditional_states.
field_semantics.writes: Required on every state. `null` where the state writes no owner artifact; otherwise the owner_artifacts key it writes.
field_semantics.grammar_surface: Required on every state whose `writes` is non-null, and absent otherwise. Names the report-format.json surface whose line_class allowlist governs THIS state's render. The binding is per state, never per artifact path (SPEC §15.5).
field_semantics.gate_id: Required on every state whose `renders_gate_declaration` is true, and absent otherwise. Names the gates/registry.json gate the state declares. A property this table exists to carry may not be read off a missing key, so the key is present on all three gate states or on none.
field_semantics.owner_reads: Declared on a WAIT whose owner must READ something before answering. AN OPEN SET, and the wording matters: `why` is the ground and is rendered in the stop's header line; EVERY OTHER KEY is an invocation the owner types, rendered in this table's own order, with `<survey record>` the one placeholder the executor substitutes. The shipped table carries `invocation`, `why`, `also` and `then` today, and adding a fifth needs no runtime change and no edit to this note. THIS SENTENCE USED TO READ "Three keys" AND ENUMERATE THEM, which is the defect kogaki#807 repaired one layer down: the renderer named `invocation` and `also`, kogaki#745 added `then`, and nothing rendered it — so a contributor adding key N+1 read a schema note promising the set was closed at three while the table already held four. The executor RENDERS every declared key at the stop and neither runs it nor relays its output — rendering the command is the hand-over, and running it would put the output back on the channel the arm exists to avoid. Data rather than driver code, and now true of the code as well as of this note.

states.does: Reads the seam once (element_survey), composes Lesson candidates and Journey marks, mints every display_id, validates, writes the survey record to the run workspace.

owner_reads.why: the owner chooses a tag from this listing, and a session's tool output is displayed to the session rather than reliably to the owner — so the act is the owner's to run (§6.0)
owner_reads.also: node src/terrain.mjs tag-rows --survey <survey record> --tag <T> — the per-tag row view, run when the owner asks to browse rows (§6.3's fork half). Never scheduled.
owner_reads.then: node src/terrain.mjs cotag-selection --survey <survey record> --tag <T> --intent "<one sentence: why these co-tags, from the model>" — §6.0.1's co-tag SELECTION display, named here once the owner has supplied the tag this stop waits for. THE INTENT PLACEHOLDER IS PART OF THE NAMED INVOCATION: it is the model's sole contribution to that surface, the executor supplies it at the invocation rather than printing it separately, and the emitter refuses it when multi-line, over 200 characters, or carrying table or marker syntax. Sited at this stop on the table's own precedent — `tag-rows` is the other owner-executed act taking `--tag <T>`, and it is named here for the same reason: both become runnable exactly when this stop's `owner_supplies` has been supplied.

states.does: Bounded tag-scoped read; emits the composition pin naming the tag, the survey pin and the member set served per group.

states.input_shape: typed claims record carrying composition_pin and one claim per group
states.refusal: claims whose group/member set is not a subset of the composition pin are refused, naming the members outside it

states.owner_supplies: adoption of the recomposed claim, the original wording kept, or free text
states.conditional: entered ONLY when a claim validated at J1_claims is pinned to a PROPER SUBSET of the member set its composition_pin served for that group. A full-group claim reaches no gate: §7 makes the full-group rendering per-invocation and not an adopted claim, so there is nothing to re-offer.
states.governing: §7, §7 (the origin travels as an argument), §7.1 (a derived origin member set announces itself), §15.4

states.input_shape: typed per-group record, judged: true, one entry per composed group, carrying the judge pin; each SubGroup carries a `coherence` label from the closed set tight | related | forced and a `coherence_why` sentence
states.refusal: a missing group entry, a bare array, or an absent judge pin is refused; a SubGroup whose `coherence` is outside the closed set, or that carries no `coherence_why`, is refused — the label is the judge's and is never defaulted here; and a judged-EMPTY outcome for a group at or above the split threshold is refused, because at that size WHETHER to split is the engine's decision rather than the judge's (§8)

states.does: Renders the co-tag screen: groups by co-tag, mints GroupIDs, renders the composed claims and the SubGroups J2 placed.
Enumerates the provenance-neighborhood's mechanical candidates for the entered set and writes them to the run workspace, so the judgment point below has something to judge.

states.input_shape: typed record keyed by candidate slug, each carrying one free-form claim and one level from the harness-fixed set
states.refusal: a level outside the closed set, a level with no claim, and a key no mechanical candidate carries are each refused, naming the offending slug

states.does: One Full Report over exactly the entered set, idempotent per §12.1's identity quadruple, carrying the provenance-neighborhood section.

states.owner_supplies: ratification of the trim, or its negation
states.conditional: entered only when a trim is proposed

states.owner_supplies: up to three Strand ids, or free text

states.does: Terminal. The flow ends here; Brief is outside the boundary and this table neither names nor guarantees a Brief launch.

screen.writer: one private screen renderer, called by the writing state the table binds it to
screen.rule: overwritten on every render; ONE writer, private to the executor (SPEC §15.5)

full_report.rule: overwritten per pull; identity is §12.1's quadruple (pin, query, judge pin, neighborhood judgment record)

owner_surface_coverage.rule: DENOMINATOR = the states in this file whose `writes` is non-null (every surviving owner surface, since §15.5 makes a writing state the only thing that may write one). NUMERATOR = those of them whose `grammar_surface` names a surface present in report-format.json's `surfaces`. A removed subcommand contributes to NEITHER term: it is not a surviving surface, so removal moves the denominator and never the numerator.
owner_surface_coverage.recomputed_never_transcribed: `at_this_version` is a convenience for a human reader and carries no authority. On any disagreement the rule above wins and the field is repaired — never the rule to the figure. No registered check executes the rule (SPEC §15.8).

bound_to_a_state.cotags: the cotag_screen state. CALLABLE for composition, REFUSED at the owner artifact: a standalone invocation whose rendering destination resolves to the repository's `reports/` fails rather than writing Screen.md (§15.5). Redirect it and the composition proceeds — a rendering whose lifetime is the run is not an owner artifact (specs/SPEC.md §2.5.1).
bound_to_a_state.report: the full_report state. Same write authority as `cotags`: callable for composition, and refused where the destination resolves to the repository's `reports/`, so FullReport.md is written only from the writing state the table binds the renderer to (§15.5).

removed_entry_points.claim: becomes J1_claims. The claims record is composed OUTSIDE the runtime and arrives as a file carrying its `composition_pin` (§15.6); the state validates it and refuses claims naming material outside the bounded read. The composition does not move into the state — only the validation does.
removed_entry_points.adopt: becomes CLAIM_REOFFER's captured answer, applied on resume (§15.6.1).
removed_entry_points.subdivide: becomes J2_subdivision, INCLUDING the composition the standalone command performed — subgroup placement from the judge's classification, the per-subgroup instruments, and the SUBDIVISION_COVER_INCOMPLETE refusal. §2.1 makes completeness a cover COUNTED IN PLACEMENTS, which is a runtime refusal; leaving it to the outside composer would move a ratified refusal out of the runtime, so the state accepts the classification record and composes under it (§15.6.2).
removed_entry_points.act: becomes TRIM_RATIFICATION's proposal record, composed by the executor when that wait is entered (`composeTrimProposal`).
removed_entry_points.gate: becomes the declaration the executor composes at any wait declaring `renders_gate_declaration: true`, through the option composer bound to that state.
removed_entry_points.capture: becomes the answer the executor records at the wait that declared the gate.

retired_entry_points.neighborhood: retired (SPEC §13.2); the section rides every `report` pull. The case survives to fail with that pointer and emits no owner surface.

non_flow_entry_points.self-test: seam-free identity-cite fixture pass; emits no owner surface, carries no sequencing authority
non_flow_entry_points.validate: runs survey-record validation; emits no owner surface

owner_executed_entry_points.tags: the pre-selection tag listing — a header and one tag row per section, under the `tag_listing` grammar. Takes `--survey <record>`; the executor names the invocation at its TAG_SELECTION stop.
owner_executed_entry_points.tag-rows: the per-tag row view — candidate rows under one named tag with their Gloss headlines, under the `tag_row_listing` grammar. Takes `--survey <record> --tag <T>`, and `--family <f>` to mark. Run when the owner asks to browse rows; never scheduled.
owner_executed_entry_points.cotag-selection: the co-tag SELECTION display (§6.0.1) — three blocks under the `cotag_selection` grammar: the fixed marker, a counts table over ALL served tags with family-named columns, and the model's one `intent:` sentence. Takes `--survey <record> --tag <T> --intent <one sentence>`. Writes NOTHING, so §15.5's write authority never engages and it is not a state; it PRECEDES the Screen and `reports/Screen.md` keeps exactly one writing state (`cotag_screen`). The executor names the invocation at its `TAG_SELECTION` stop, intent placeholder included, and neither runs it nor relays its output.

entry_point_accounting: EVERY case in src/terrain.mjs's dispatcher appears in exactly one of the 5 maps above (bound_to_a_state, removed_entry_points, retired_entry_points, non_flow_entry_points, owner_executed_entry_points), and THAT TOTALITY is the property rather than the count: the next entry point is covered by the totality rather than by having been remembered. A case in none of them, or in two, is a defect against this file.
